lists.name: Grade 1 — Things at School
lists.description: Everyday words from the classroom and the schoolyard. Each word has a simple meaning and a sentence to read aloud.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: A tool with graphite inside that you use to write or draw
words.example: I sharpened my pencil before the spelling test.

words.definition: A table where a student sits and works
words.example: My name is written on the top of my desk.

words.definition: A small rubber piece that rubs out pencil marks
words.example: Use the eraser if you make a mistake.

words.definition: A person you like and enjoy spending time with
words.example: My best friend sits next to me at lunch.

words.definition: A stick of colored wax used for drawing
words.example: She drew a rainbow with a red crayon.

words.definition: A straight tool used to measure length or draw straight lines
words.example: Measure the line with a ruler, not with your fingers.

words.definition: Thin sheets used for writing, drawing, or printing
words.example: Please put your name at the top of the paper.

words.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the school day
words.example: I packed a cheese sandwich for lunch today.

words.definition: A person who helps students learn at school
words.example: Our teacher reads a story every morning.

words.definition: A room full of books that you can borrow
words.example: We visit the library every Friday to choose a book.

words.definition: A seat with a back, meant for one person
words.example: Please push your chair under the table when you leave.

words.definition: A bag you wear on your back to carry school things
words.example: My backpack felt heavy with all my books.

words.definition: A sticky liquid that holds paper or other things together
words.example: Use a little glue to stick the picture on the card.

words.definition: A break from class when children play outside
words.example: At recess we played tag on the big field.

words.definition: Work that students finish at home after school
words.example: I finished my homework before dinner.

words.definition: A pen with thick, colored ink
words.example: The teacher wrote the date on the board with a black marker.

lists.name: Grade 9 — How Governments Work
lists.description: Words from civics and history about voting, laws and how countries are run. Each word has a plain meaning and a sentence about a real situation.
lists.subject: history

words.definition: To choose a leader or make a decision by casting a ballot
words.example: Every citizen over eighteen can vote in the election.

words.definition: A rule that everyone in a country must follow
words.example: It is against the law to drive through a red light.

words.definition: A large group of people who share a country, history, and language
words.example: The nation celebrated its independence with parades.

words.definition: A person who belongs to a country and has its rights
words.example: Every citizen has the right to a fair trial.

words.definition: A system where people choose their leaders through voting
words.example: In a democracy, the people decide who runs the government.

words.definition: A country led by elected leaders instead of a king
words.example: The country became a republic after the king gave up power.

words.definition: The basic set of rules that defines how a country is governed
words.example: The constitution protects freedom of speech.

words.definition: A change added to a constitution or a law
words.example: The amendment gave women the right to vote.

words.definition: A formal agreement signed by two or more countries
words.example: The two countries signed a peace treaty in 1919.

words.definition: A place ruled by people from another country
words.example: The colony wanted to govern itself after many years.

words.definition: A sudden, large change in government, often by force
words.example: The revolution changed the country's laws forever.

words.definition: An official count of all the people living in a country
words.example: The census counts how many people live in each city.

words.definition: The group of people in a country who make the laws
words.example: The legislature debated the new tax law for weeks.

words.definition: The power of a country to govern itself
words.example: The country fought hard to protect its sovereignty.

words.definition: To officially approve an agreement or a constitution
words.example: The states voted to ratify the new constitution.

words.definition: A leader's power to stop a law from passing
words.example: The president decided to veto the bill.

lists.name: Grade 11 — Words for People and Ideas
lists.description: Precise words for describing character, arguments and thinking. Each word comes with a clear definition and a sentence that shows how it is used.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: Telling the truth and not hiding anything
words.example: An honest answer is better than a clever lie.

words.definition: Short in length or time
words.example: The coach gave a brief talk before the game.

words.definition: Paying close attention to avoid mistakes or harm
words.example: She was careful not to spill the paint.

words.definition: Relaxed and not upset, even under pressure
words.example: The pilot stayed calm during the storm.

words.definition: Open and direct, even when the truth is uncomfortable
words.example: He gave me a candid review of my essay.

words.definition: Speaking or writing in a clear, graceful, and powerful way
words.example: The eloquent speaker won the whole room over.

words.definition: Dealing with problems in a practical, realistic way
words.example: The team chose a pragmatic plan instead of an ideal one.

words.definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty
words.example: Young children are often more resilient than adults expect.

words.definition: Doubting a claim until there is good proof
words.example: The judge was skeptical of the witness's story.

words.definition: Showing great attention to every small detail
words.example: The engineer was meticulous about every measurement.

words.definition: Able to convince others to believe or do something
words.example: Her persuasive argument changed everyone's mind.

words.definition: Unwilling to do something and hesitant about it
words.example: He was reluctant to admit that he had lost.

words.definition: Expressing a lot in only a few words
words.example: A good summary is short and concise.

words.definition: Kind and wanting to help other people
words.example: The benevolent old man shared his food with anyone who asked.

words.definition: Found everywhere at the same time
words.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.

words.definition: Clear and easy to understand
words.example: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the theorem.

lists.name: Grade 12 — Money and the Economy
lists.description: The money words you meet in real life and in economics class, from saving a few coins to national prices. Each word has a clear meaning and a sentence to show it in use.
lists.subject: general

words.definition: Coins and notes that people use to buy things
words.example: I saved my money to buy a new bike.

words.definition: The amount of money someone pays for something
words.example: The price of bread went up this year.

words.definition: Regular work that a person does to earn money
words.example: My aunt got a new job at the hospital.

words.definition: Money kept aside for later use
words.example: Our savings will pay for the trip next summer.

words.definition: A plan for how much money to spend and how much to save
words.example: We made a budget for groceries each month.

words.definition: Money a business keeps after paying its costs
words.example: The shop made a profit this year.

words.definition: Money that a person owes to someone else
words.example: He finally paid off his debt to the bank.

words.definition: Money paid to a worker for their work
words.example: The new wage helps families pay the rent.

words.definition: A place or system where goods are bought and sold
words.example: The farmers sold fresh vegetables at the market.

words.definition: The amount of a product that is available to buy
words.example: When the supply of corn is low, prices rise.

words.definition: How many people want to buy a product
words.example: High demand for the game sold out the stock.

words.definition: To put money into something to earn more money later
words.example: She decided to invest in a small company.

words.definition: Extra money paid for borrowing or for keeping money in a bank
words.example: The bank paid interest on my savings account.

words.definition: A general rise in prices over time
words.example: Inflation means your money buys less than it did before.

words.definition: A tax on goods brought into a country from abroad
words.example: The government added a tariff on imported steel.

words.definition: A situation where spending is larger than the money coming in
words.example: The country ran a deficit after the expensive war.
